items.question: What condition of death and splendor arises for the accomplished practitioner?
premises: Death does not occur for him
His splendor is imperishable
His splendor is immortal
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner transcends death and possesses imperishable immortal splendor.
items.plain_english: For him there is no death; indeed his splendor is imperishable and immortal.

items.question: What power does the accomplished practitioner wield when angered, O goddess?
premises: The practitioner can become angered
He can shake the three worlds
The three worlds include moving and unmoving beings
items.inference: When angered, the accomplished practitioner has the power to shake the entire threefold world.
items.plain_english: But when angered, O goddess, he can shake the three worlds with all their moving and unmoving beings.

items.question: What is the essential means by which such accomplishment arises?
premises: Accomplishment arises in a certain manner
Constant practice is the means
Constant practice alone is emphasized
items.inference: Whatever kind of accomplishment arises, it arises through constant practice alone.
items.plain_english: Whatever kind of accomplishment arises, it comes about indeed through constant practice.

items.question: How is this knowledge characterized in relation to autonomy and accomplishment?
premises: This is knowledge
It is supreme knowledge
It is the mind of autonomy and accomplishment
items.inference: This knowledge is the supreme knowledge, consisting in the mind of autonomy and accomplishment.
items.plain_english: This is the supreme knowledge, the knowledge that is the mind of autonomy and accomplishment.

items.question: How should one who desires accomplishment receive this knowledge in the Kaula path?
premises: This knowledge must be taken
It must be taken with effort
The seeker desires accomplishment in the Kaula path
items.inference: One who desires accomplishment in the Kaula path should receive this knowledge with effort.
uncertainties: kaulave could refer to a Kaula context or a Kaula practitioner
items.plain_english: One who desires accomplishment in the Kaula path should receive this with effort.

items.question: What physical and mental practice is prescribed for directing the mind?
premises: The tongue should be turned upward
The mind should be fixed there
These actions are performed together
items.inference: One should turn the tongue upward and fix the mind there.
items.plain_english: Having turned the tongue upward, one should fix the mind there.

items.question: What immediate freedom results from the prescribed yogic practice?
premises: Freedom occurs in a moment
One is freed from diseases
These include illness, death, old age, and others
items.inference: Through this practice one is instantly freed from diseases, including illness, death, old age, and the like.
items.plain_english: In a moment one is freed from diseases, from illness, death, old age, and so forth.

items.question: What specific curative effect arises instantly in the pungent experience?
premises: Disease is destroyed in a moment
This occurs in the pungent state
The effect includes the destruction of leprosy
items.inference: In the pungent experience, disease is instantly destroyed, including leprosy.
uncertainties: kaṭuke may refer to a pungent taste or a specific yogic state
items.plain_english: In a moment disease is destroyed in the pungent state, bringing the destruction of leprosy.

items.question: What transformation occurs in a person through the experience of milk taste?
premises: The experience is of milk taste
A man becomes wise
A man becomes immortal
items.inference: Through the taste of milk, a man becomes wise and immortal.
uncertainties: kṣīra+svādena may refer to a literal taste or a yogic nectar experience
items.plain_english: By the taste of milk, a man becomes wise and immortal.

rows.grounds: object or state to be placed

items.question: Where should the mind and the yawning state be directed in this practice?
premises: The mind should be placed in the circle
Placement is also directed to the nose
Yawning should be placed or induced there
items.inference: One should place the mind in the circle and direct yawning in the nose.
uncertainties: cakreṇa and vijṛmbhikā have ambiguous roles in this compressed instruction
items.plain_english: One should place the mind in the circle, and place yawning in the nose.

items.question: What exalted beings or status may the practitioner attain through this practice?
premises: Divine maidens of the gods are involved
The status of yakṣa or vidyādhara is possible
Such attainment may occur
items.inference: The practitioner may attain association with divine maidens and become like a yakṣa or vidyādhara.
uncertainties: deva+kanyā may be subject or object in this compressed verse
items.plain_english: He may become associated with divine maidens of the gods and become a yakṣa or vidyādhara.

items.question: What enjoyment with divine maidens is promised to the practitioner, O beloved?
premises: Many divine maidens are attracted
Attraction precedes enjoyment
Enjoyment takes place
items.inference: Having attracted many divine maidens, they enjoy them, O beloved.
uncertainties: subject of bhuñjate is implied from context
items.plain_english: Having attracted many divine maidens, they enjoy them, O beloved.

items.question: What distinction is made between a true yogin and one who is not, O beloved?
premises: A yogin becomes one whose seed flows upward
Another is not a true yogin
A manual act is contrasted
items.inference: The true yogin is one whose seed flows upward, not one defined by a manual act, O beloved.
uncertainties: karata(? is an uncertain or corrupt reading
exact contrast implied by karata(? is unclear
items.plain_english: The yogin becomes one whose seed flows upward; he is not a yogin by hand, O beloved.

items.question: How rare and supreme is this circle compared to other yogic practices?
premises: This circle is difficult to obtain
No yoga is higher than this
Its supremacy is asserted
items.inference: This circle is difficult to obtain and there is no yoga higher than this.
items.plain_english: This circle is indeed difficult to obtain; there is no yoga higher than this.

items.question: What effect does step-by-step training in this practice produce?
premises: Practice is undertaken step by step
The practice is well trained
It causes great wonder
items.inference: When practiced step by step, this discipline produces great wonder.
items.plain_english: When practiced step by step, it becomes a cause of great wonder.

items.question: What certainty is assured for those devoted to constant practice?
premises: There is no doubt here
The result is assured
Practitioners are devoted to constant practice
items.inference: For those devoted to constant practice, there is no doubt about this result.
items.plain_english: There is no doubt here for those devoted to constant practice.

items.question: What extraordinary power manifests during muttering focused on the image?
premises: Muttering occurs in relation to the image
This takes place in that context
Breaking of pots and stones occurs
items.inference: In that muttering focused on the image, the power to break pots and stones manifests.
uncertainties: pratimā+jalpanan is a compressed expression with unclear exact nuance
items.plain_english: In that muttering before the image, there is the breaking of pots and stones.

items.question: Which great deities are included among those encompassed by this vision or power?
premises: Brahma, Viṣṇu, Yama, and Indra are included
Varuṇa is included
Vāyu is included
items.inference: The list of encompassed deities includes Brahma, Viṣṇu, Yama, Indra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu.
items.plain_english: Brahma, Viṣṇu, Yama, and Indra, and also Varuṇa and Vāyu.

items.question: Which other classes of beings are included in this encompassing vision, O beloved?
premises: Gandharvas are included
Kinnaras, Yakṣas, and Nāgas are included
Vidyādharas are included
items.inference: The encompassing vision also includes Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Nāgas, and Vidyādharas.
items.plain_english: Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Nāgas, and Vidyādharas, O beloved.

items.question: What cosmic totality is encompassed within the scope of this realization?
premises: The cosmos is endowed with constellations and stars
The entire universe is encompassed
This totality is presented as an object
items.inference: The realization encompasses the entire universe, endowed with constellations and stars.
items.plain_english: The universe, endowed with constellations and stars, encompassed as a whole.

items.question: How can the practitioner manifest his own body through constant meditation?
premises: Constant meditation is the means
One's own body can be shown
It can be shown in many ways
items.inference: Through constant meditation, the practitioner can manifest his own body in many ways.
items.plain_english: Through constant meditation, he may show his own body in many ways.

items.question: What kind of accomplishment is granted through practice according to scripture?
premises: Accomplishment arises from practice
It is eightfold
It is enjoined by scripture
items.inference: From practice comes the eightfold accomplishment enjoined by scripture.
items.plain_english: From practice comes the eightfold accomplishment enjoined by scripture.

items.question: To whom should this Kaula teaching be given and to whom withheld?
premises: This Kaula teaching should be given to the worthy
It should not be given to just anyone
Discrimination in transmission is required
items.inference: This Kaula teaching must be given only to the worthy and not to anyone at random.
items.plain_english: This Kaula teaching should be given to the worthy, and not given to just anyone.

items.question: What attitude of secrecy and resolve is required regarding this extraction?
premises: This extraction must be concealed
It must be concealed always
One must be firmly resolved
items.inference: This extraction must always be kept secret by one who is firmly resolved.
uncertainties: etat+uddharaṇaṃ may refer to an extracted essence or a specific teaching
items.plain_english: This extraction must always be kept secret by one who is firmly resolved.
